title: Living ashtpadi 3
hookLine: the Name first, and deeds to match it

lines: THE GAP BETWEEN WORD AND DEED.
cards: Let's get coffee soon, says the friend, and the coffee never happens. A company's website is full of the word integrity. A Sunday-night promise: this week will be different.

Words are easy. They cost nothing until someone has to live inside them, and being let down by words that never became deeds is its own small ache. The third ashtpadi of Sukhmani is, in the end, about closing that gap.

teach.h: THE SALOK, THE LIST, THE LADDER.
teach.b: Gather the third ashtpadi. Its salok: I have searched many scriptures, and nothing equals the Name.
Its long list: chanting, fasting, ritual, pilgrimage, forest, fire; none equal reflecting on the Name, because washing the body doesn't wash the mind.
And its final ladder: the highest way is to chant the Name and do pure deeds. Side by side, a shape appears.
The ashtpadi is suspicious of outside without inside, the ritual done while pride sits untouched. But it's just as clear that the inside has to come out. The Name first, then deeds to match.
Nirmal karam, clean action, sits beside remembering at the top of the ladder. Guru Nanak puts it in one line in Sri Raag.
In paraphrase: truth is higher than everything, but higher still is truthful living. Not truth as an idea you agree with; truth as a way you live.
On an ordinary day, that's the Name on your lips in the morning, and the same Name visible in how you treat the cashier, the coworker, the person in the next car.
Sikh teaching builds this into everyday life: naam japna, remembering the Name, sits next to kirat karni, honest work, and vand chhakna, sharing what you have.
Remembering, earning, sharing: words and deeds, together.

how: Sikh teaching pairs naam japna (remembering God) with kirat karni (honest work) and vand chhakna (sharing), so that remembrance shows up in action.

o: action, deeds: what you actually do
a promise spoken aloud to others
fate, the luck you're simply born with

games.q: word and deed — tap the pairs.

s: the third ashtpadi says remembering is enough without action
the Name sits beside pure deeds at the top of its ladder.
Guru Nanak said truthful living is higher still than truth
Sri Raag, Ang 62: truthful living is higher still.
Sikh life pairs remembering with honest work and sharing
naam japna, kirat karni, vand chhakna.

games.q: you told a friend you'd help them move, and the day is here. what does living the third ashtpadi look like?
o: show up and help, the Name in your heart.
send a kind message and stay in.
games.why: the Name first, and deeds to match it: truthful living is higher still.

practice: Think of something you've said recently and haven't done yet, I'll call you, I'll help with that, and hold it in mind for a breath, without guilt, just looking at it.
Then picture the one small step that would make the word true, and if you pray, say Waheguru once and let the word and the deed meet.

wordCard.voice: Karam, action: Sukhmani's third section in daily life, the Name first, and deeds to match it, because truthful living is higher still.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: karam, action; Sukhmani pairs the Name with nirmal karam, pure action.

carryVoice: Your line: say it, do it. The call you promised can still happen. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sri Raag M1, Ang 62 (truth and truthful living)
